Lessons.Title: The Size of Angles in Degrees
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will understand that angles can be measured in degrees and use benchmark angle measurements to make sense of the new unit.
Previously, you used the hands of an analog clock to describe and compare the size of angles. In this lesson, you learn about degrees as a unit for measuring angles. In the first activity, you are introduced to 360 degrees as the measurement of a full rotation of a ray about a fixed point.

2021 lesson activities: Warm-up: What Do You Know about 360? (10 minutes); Activity 1: A Full Turn (15 minutes); Activity 2: Make a Measuring Tool (20 minutes); Cool-down: Estimate Angle Size in Degrees (5 minutes)
Corrected mathematical focus: A full turn is 360°; benchmarks 90°, 180°, and 270° are quarter, half and three-quarter turns.

Edulytics authored guidance: Divide a 360-degree full turn into four equal parts of 90 degrees. Use a 120° angle as one third of a full turn. Place the benchmark angle into the source measuring-tool model.
First-party Cool-down (not publisher assessment): What fraction of a full turn is 270°?
Images, drawing/protractor accuracy, partner tasks and the gated original publisher Cool-down require original task evidence and teacher/visual review.
